item.title: UFC 333's 7 big questions: Is the Alex Volkanovski era over? Which Yan-Dvalishvili fight was a fluke?
item.description: If you like immense technical skill, unheralded prowess, and festering vendettas, UFC 333 might just be your huckleberry. There will be two titles on the line, featuring some of the most technically sound fighters on the UFC's roster. There will also be storylines galore. In the main event on Saturday from Abu Dhabi, perhaps the greatest featherweight that ever lived, Alexander Volkanovski, goes head-to-head with the dominant (and dangerously unsung) Movsar Evloev , which checks every box of fascination. Can Evloev actually win on the scorecards against a master in-cage conductor like the 38-year-old "Volk," who is trying for his seventh overall title defense? Can Evloev finish Volkanovski? Or does the old dog humble the Russian challenger? In the co-main, it's a trilogy fight between one of the most prolific champions of the era (Merab Dvalishvili) and 135 pounds of Georgian kryptonite (current champ, Petr Yan) . It's time to get right down to it and ask the seven burning questions for UFC 333. 1. True or false: Excluding Islam Makhachev, Movsar Evloev is the toughest challenge Volkanovski has faced? Evloev is 20-0, has an incredibly effective style and, perhaps most importantly, the UFC has appeared to be utterly allergic to putting him in a title fight — a clear mark of greatness (ask Kamaru Usman, Leon Edwards and Belal Muhammad). The problem is, unlike Dana White's maiden year with Zuffa Boxing, we don't have to wait until the end of 2026 to judge "Volk's" body of work — it's already set in stone. He fought Ilia Topuria, Max Holloway, Jose Aldo, and the aforementioned Islam Makhachev — all while they were in their primes. I'm as big an Evloev fan as the next guy, but I'm pumping the brakes on this one. What's more likely to happen: Evloev actually finishes Alexander ‘The Great,’ or Volkanovski wins a decision against a scorecard master? Chuck: You know, Petesy, I am leaning toward the latter here for a couple of reasons. For one, Volkanovski doesn't get outfoxed or outworked for very long in a given fight, and in fact, he almost always ends up dictating the dance. Even against an iron-willed Russian, it's hard for me to imagine "Volk" being whittled away through five rounds. The other thing is: I think Evloev, out of spite, would like to prove he can outlast Volkanovski for 25 minutes, which is a subplot to this featured fight . I think he'd feel extremely uncomfortable if he was presented with a red carpet to Volkanovski's chin, or if he saw a neck sitting there to be snatched. The one thing I will say is that at 38 years old, you never know when the wheels might come off. I know "Volk" works hard and his fight IQ is unparalleled (poor Diego Lopes found out about that … twice ), but age can become a factor overnight. Petesy: As a 39-year-old male, I can attest to this. My wheels came off back in 2005, so it's something that "Volk" needs to be aware of. I agree with you on this one. If Evloev and Volkanovski have something in common, it's the glee they exude while watching another man wilt before them. However, even though it was a successful outing, Evloev showed he can be bent by constant pressure against Lerone Murphy. Similarly with Merab Dvalishvili in his last outing against Petr Yan (we can circle back to this), Evloev fought Murphy in brass-pleasing fashion, throwing away his monotonous grappling style for something more fan friendly. For me, it would be a terrible idea for him to go away from his A-game against Volkanovski. If he does, I could see "Volk" stopping him. That said, I think a Volkanovski decision is the most likely outcome. Could UFC 333 be Alexander Volkanovski's last dance? Mark Metcalfe via Getty Images 3. Is there a chance Volkanovski retires after this fight? And under what circumstances would he consider it? Petesy: Plainly, no. Why don't I think he will? Well, because he is in the perfect position to do so. The fight game isn't that easy. I watched "Volk" pitch a retirement fight against Justin Gaethje in the lead-up to this bout. Although it wouldn't make the slightest bit of sense for the UFC to a host a double-retirement bout, as Volkanovksi suggested, it certainly shows his intent to continue. Even if he loses, I don't think he's the kind of guy who would want to go out on a loss. And let's not forget about the revelations we heard ahead of the short-notice Makhachev rematch. Unfortunately, I'm pretty confident "Volk," like many, will struggle to call it a day when the time comes. Chuck: Yeah, Volkanovski's talk around the (crammed) Islam rematch is what makes me think he won't be able to call it a day so easily. If he beats Evloev, we will be talking about this guy as something of a godsend to fighterkind, a 38-year-old former rugby player who somehow strung together one of the greatest résumés in the annals of UFC history. Just up and leave at a moment like that ? Not bloody likely. You think he doesn't hear Jean Silva barking from the neighbor's yard? Oh, he hears it all right. And he has a dog biscuit in his back pocket just for the occasion, Petesy. If "Volk" loses, and loses badly, there's a part of me that thinks he might consider it. I think there's been a switch in mindset with him, and he's tailor-made to segue into coaching for his vicarious competition fix. He also has a level head (not to mention some comedy chops), which makes me think he might be more rational about the right time to walk away than we give him credit for. Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili are ready for Round 3. Chris Unger via Getty Images 4. I didn't think that Merab put the right emphasis (or concern) on that last fight with Yan, that he showed up somewhat … to use the word that scared Georges St-Pierre so much for all those years … complacent . In that way, I saw that fight — especially at that time — as somewhat of a distortion of the truth. Then again, as time has gone on, I think that's the devil sitting on my shoulder. The angel on the other one wants to praise Yan for a masterful performance in that last fight, for confounding and bewitching and ultimately battering Merab for four of the five rounds. item.title: French teenage rugby player dies after on-field injury
item.description: Clea Menier was playing for Union du Bassin Marmandais Under-18s [FFR] A 17-year-old amateur rugby player has died after suffering an on-field injury during a match in France. Clea Menier - a back row for Union du Bassin Marmandais - died after what her club said was an "accident" during an under-18s match against Agen Agglo Rugby on Saturday. After receiving medical attention on the field, the teenager was taken to Pellegrin Hospital in Bordeaux, where she died from her injuries. Neither the club nor the French Rugby Federation (FFR) have disclosed the nature of her injury. "It is with immense sadness and indescribable pain that Union du Bassin Marmandais learned of the death of Clea," the club said in a statement, which paid tribute to the emergency services who treated her. "We are also thinking of her loved ones and friends, whose immense pain we share, as well as her team-mates, coaches, and everyone who had the privilege of knowing her and sharing their passion for rugby with her. "This is a terrible ordeal for our club. We will get through it together - united, standing in solidarity, and looking after one another." The FFR said: "This loss has deeply shaken the entire rugby family. "In these moments of sadness, the FFR wishes to express its full support and solidarity to Clea's family and loved ones. "It also extends its sincerest condolences to her team-mates, coaches, and all members of Union du Bassin Marmandais. "Every effort will be made to understand the circumstances surrounding this accident."

He has a nasty uppercut, and Kuniev tends to rely on a high guard. If he presses forward with the occasional combo, catching Kuniev ducking might be his best chance at a finish. How Kuniev Wins Kuniev has proven himself extremely difficult to take down in his trio of UFC fights. On the feet, he’s primarily a boxer, possessing quick hands and good counter timing. item.title: Countdown to Frankfurt at home: facts, kits, TV coverage
item.description: Countdown to Frankfurt at home: facts, kits, TV coverage Head-to-head record: Goals galore in recent meetings When Borussia Dortmund and Eintracht Frankfurt met last season, both matches produced plenty of goals. After a 3-3 draw in the first meeting, BVB claimed a 3-2 home win in the reverse fixture last May. Their overall home record against the Eagles from Frankfurt is very good. The Black & Yellows have won all five of their most recent home games against Eintracht Frankfurt. In total, they have recorded 39 Bundesliga home wins against SGE, alongside six draws and eight defeats. Kits: BVB in yellow Borussia Dortmund will wear their yellow home shirts with black shorts and yellow socks ( visit the online shop ). SGE will play in their white away shirts. Referee: Jablonski in charge Sven Jablonski will referee the match. His assistant referees will be Eduard Beitinger and Dr Martin Thomsen. Felix Bickel will be the fourth official, with Sören Storks acting as video assistant referee. Broadcast: Live on Sky The match will be shown live on Sky Sport Bundesliga, with coverage starting at 17:30. The game will be streamed live on WOW . Wolff-Christoph Fuss will provide commentary. Attendance: A full house The floodlit match is sold out, with all 81,365 tickets snapped up. More than 7,000 away fans are expected from Frankfurt. Tickets: Resale platform open Anyone who wants to be at SIGNAL IDUNA PARK but does not yet have a ticket has a chance to secure one through BVB's official ticket resale platform. Ticket holders who cannot attend in person can legally offer their season ticket or match ticket for resale in the BVB ticket shop until two and a half hours before kick-off. There is no need to physically hand over the ticket, as it is electronically deactivated and then reactivated for its new holder. Weather: Autumn chill Temperatures in Dortmund are forecast to reach no higher than ten degrees on Saturday evening. At least it should remain largely dry around the time of the match. Your match ticket includes the DSW21 combined ticket for travel to and from the match on public transport throughout North Rhine-Westphalia. This also applies to holders of plastic season ticket cards. Holders of Print@Home tickets or mobile tickets must carry a separate public transport ticket in addition to their match ticket. This can be ordered free of charge online on this page . All further travel information for the match against Eintracht Frankfurt. BVB channels: All the match information On matchday, BVB will keep fans up to date across all its digital channels: Live ticker In the BVB app's “Matchday Mode” ( download here ), you can find news, photos, posts, videos, statistics and much more about the match from 09:09 until after the final whistle. From kick-off, the live ticker will cover all the key moments. Netradio Listen on the homepage and in the BVB app on iPhone and Android devices . item.title: Ole Miss vs Texas: A CFB27 simulation
item.description: FRISCO, TX - FEBRUARY 01: Ole mIss helmet sits during the East-West Shrine Bowl game on February 1, 2024 at the Ford Center at the star in Frisco, TX. (Photo by Chris Leduc/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images So far this season, EA has the Rebels undefeated and projected a 19 point victory over Missouri last weekend. While it was an even more impressive showing by the real life Rebs, the video game simulated season hasn’t been all that off. Now the biggest test of the season lies ahead of the Rebels. On the road, against a desperate Texas team. It’s a similar situation in the video game as Ole Miss heads to a two-loss Texas. 1st Quarter Opening scripts seem to be a weakness of the staff, but it sure didn’t translate to this virtual contest. Ok maybe it wasn’t the script, but more Trinidad being a super hero as he broke off a 69 yard run to begin the game. That run set up a quick Kewan Lacy touchdown. The Longhorns went three and out and Chambliss drove the Rebs down the field again. This time, former Longhorn Johntay Cook snagged a 15 yard touchdown pass. On the final drive of the first quarter, Texas was able to sustain a long drive, leading to a Raleek Brown 9 yard touchdown run. End 1st: 14-7 Ole Miss 2nd Quarter The Ole Miss offense stayed hot to open the second quarter as Kewan Lacy scored from 28 yards out, putting the Rebs up 21-7. Raleek Brown fumbled on the next Texas possession, leading to a Lucas Carneiro 38 yard field goal. Arch Manning was able to break loose on a 65 yard run to answer back and that was it for first half action. End of 2nd: 24-14 Ole Miss 3rd Quarter Arch Manning wasn’t done running. It’s as if the Ole Miss defense was focused on stopping the running backs, they were unsure who was to take Manning. Arch ran another one in to draw Texas within a field goal. The next Rebel drive ended as quickly as it began with Texas sacking Chambliss for a safety, pulling within one point. Ole Miss had to punt it back to Texas, only for Hollywood Smothers to break off a 43 yard run, ending the scoring for the quarter. End of 3rd: 30-24 Texas 4th Quarter Chambliss was able to answer, as he often does. After driving down the field, Trinidad connected with Horatio Fields for a 19 yard score. Trailing in the fourth quarter with Arch Manning as their quarterback has been a rollercoaster ride for Texas fans. Down by one in this game, Manning was able to find Cam Coleman for a 42 yard score. Texas missed the extra point, bringing the score to 36-31 Texas. For perhaps the first time ever, Chambliss wasn’t clutch. He was intercepted, which led to another Longhorn touchdown, slamming the door shut and leading to the first virtual loss on the season. Final: 43-31 Texas Story of the Stats Trinidad Chambliss finished with 299 passing yards and 100 rushing yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Arch Manning threw for 218, but ran for 165 for a total of three scores himself. Hollywood Smothers added 120 yards

While it was an even more impressive showing by the real life Rebs, the video game simulated season hasn’t been all that off. Now the biggest test of the season lies ahead of the Rebels. On the road, against a desperate Texas team. It’s a similar situation in the video game as Ole Miss heads to a two-loss Texas. 1st Quarter Opening scripts seem to be a weakness of the staff, but it sure didn’t translate to this virtual contest. Ok maybe it wasn’t the script, but more Trinidad being a super hero as he broke off a 69 yard run to begin the game. That run set up a quick Kewan Lacy touchdown. The Longhorns went three and out and Chambliss drove the Rebs down the field again. This time, former Longhorn Johntay Cook snagged a 15 yard touchdown pass. On the final drive of the first quarter, Texas was able to sustain a long drive, leading to a Raleek Brown 9 yard touchdown run. End 1st: 14-7 Ole Miss 2nd Quarter The Ole Miss offense stayed hot to open the second quarter as Kewan Lacy scored from 28 yards out, putting the Rebs up 21-7. Raleek Brown fumbled on the next Texas possession, leading to a Lucas Carneiro 38 yard field goal. Arch Manning was able to break loose on a 65 yard run to answer back and that was it for first half action. End of 2nd: 24-14 Ole Miss 3rd Quarter Arch Manning wasn’t done running. It’s as if the Ole Miss defense was focused on stopping the running backs, they were unsure who was to take Manning. Arch ran another one in to draw Texas within a field goal. The next Rebel drive ended as quickly as it began with Texas sacking Chambliss for a safety, pulling within one point. Ole Miss had to punt it back to Texas, only for Hollywood Smothers to break off a 43 yard run, ending the scoring for the quarter. End of 3rd: 30-24 Texas 4th Quarter Chambliss was able to answer, as he often does. After driving down the field, Trinidad connected with Horatio Fields for a 19 yard score. Trailing in the fourth quarter with Arch Manning as their quarterback has been a rollercoaster ride for Texas fans. Down by one in this game, Manning was able to find Cam Coleman for a 42 yard score. Texas missed the extra point, bringing the score to 36-31 Texas. For perhaps the first time ever, Chambliss wasn’t clutch. He was intercepted, which led to another Longhorn touchdown, slamming the door shut and leading to the first virtual loss on the season. Final: 43-31 Texas Story of the Stats Trinidad Chambliss finished with 299 passing yards and 100 rushing yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Arch Manning threw for 218, but ran for 165 for a total of three scores himself. Hollywood Smothers added 120 yards on 16 carries. Deuce Alexander was the leading receiver in the game, finishing with 136 yards on nine receptions, but was unable to break off one his patented explosive plays. Will Echoles had two more sacks in this game. Texas had 300 yards rushing, contributing to 571 total yards. They converted 61% of their third downs, won the turnover battle and had 10 more minutes than Ole Miss in time of possession.

item.title: Nottingham Forest handed big boost ahead of Ipswich clash
item.description: Nottingham Forest handed big boost ahead of Ipswich clash Oliver Glasner has confirmed Morgan Gibbs-White will return for Nottingham Forest’s Premier League trip to Ipswich Town. The England midfielder missed the weekend defeat to Arsenal after picking up a knock against Crystal Palace, with Forest opting not to risk him after he struggled to train in the build-up. But Glasner says Gibbs-White has now trained throughout the week and is available to start. “He’s ready, he trained the entire week, so there are no issues,” the Forest boss said. “Nikola Milenković was already on the bench and is ready to start and play. “It’s just Igor Jesus and Nicolò Savona who can’t be involved in the matchday squad, but all the others are fine and fit.” Glasner also highlighted the importance of having Gibbs-White back available, while stressing Forest cannot rely on their captain alone. “Of course, when your captain is available, it’s important,” he said. “It’s someone who can create chances and score goals himself. “That’s positive, but I think you could also see that without Morgan Gibbs-White, we had a very competitive team against the champions. “This gives us confidence because we lost without Morgan and with Morgan. “He’s an important part, but he can’t win the game alone, so we need a top team performance, but it’s good to have him back.”

His quotes are tactically dense so warrant breaking down, but what did Fernandes mean, and does he have a point? Since Michael Carrick became United manager in January, they have largely defended in a zonal 4-2-4 or 4-4-2 shape that springs into a press in moments. Here we see United's 4-2-4 shape in the first half against Como yesterday [BBC] At times during Carrick's stint as caretaker head coach last season, it worked well - as we saw when Bryan Mbeumo scored in United's 3-2 win at Arsenal in January two weeks after Carrick took over But the same approach has been less effective this season. On the same night defender Lisandro Martinez questioned United's recruitment - after their 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid - he also spoke about the ever-changing tactical landscape. "You can't stay with what you did last season." he said. "Teams know you, how you play, know every detail, and if you don't change, next season is a big problem." Last season, the introduction of the 4-2-4 shape as a defensive tactic caught a number of teams off guard, making it more effective. Pep Guardiola and Pep Lijnders used the same shape at Manchester City - a tweak that underpinned their Carabao Cup final win over an ill-prepared Arsenal. Having replaced Guardiola, Enzo Maresca redeployed it for the Community Shield in August, but this time Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta had the solutions and the Gunners won. Within a few games, Maresca had abandoned the 4-24 and moved to a more man-to-man style of defending. In their recent game against PSG, City took a far more man-to-man approach behind the ball. Guehi is seen stepping out of defence to track his man. [BBC] Perhaps that is the sort of change Fernandes is hoping for - recognising the reduced effectiveness of United's defensive approach, with signs of weakness visible as early as pre-season. AC Milan - now managed by former United boss Ruben Amorim - repeatedly found joy playing around the 4-2-4, with a back five that outnumbered the Red Devils' front four. United's two central attackers would look to block passes into Milan's midfield two before pressing the central defenders. The wide position of one of the central defenders would force a United winger to step out, and Milan's wing-back - dropping deep and wide - gave them an easy way out. United's full-back would then have to cover a large distance to close down the wing-back but by the time pressure was applied, the ball was gone. Milan accessed the wide areas well around United's front four resulting in the midfielders or full-back having to cover large distances [BBC] The same problems were seen in United's defeat by Atletico Madrid. Atletico took the risk of employing the same tactic with a back four rather than a back five, which left them an extra attacker high up the pitch. As United's front two looked to stop passes into the central midfielders, the wide position of the centre-backs drew out United's wingers. That, in turn, meant left-back Alejandro Grimaldo found himself in space out wide. This required Diogo Dalot, or if he was pinned back by winger Alex Baena, Youri Tielemans to cover large distances in an attempt to apply some pressure to Grimaldo. So while Fernandes may have been referring to himself when he said "they make you run a lot, people get frustrated", it could easily have applied to these team-mates. Atletico Madrid used a back four, bravely splitting their centre-backs, accessing the full-back around United's front four. This forced Dalot, in this example, to jump to press Grimaldo. Given the distance, he was unable to apply meaningful pressure. [BBC] Why is Carrick taking this approach? When Fernandes' quotes were put to Carrick after the game, he pushed back. "We actually half-pressed, man-to-man in the second half and then ended up conceding a goal from that," he said. "It's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, but if you don't run and you don't run forward and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." While the less aggressive 4-2-4 has its weaknesses, it often leaves an extra player in the backline, giving United a numerical advantage in defence. It also aims to funnel attacks down the flanks, where they are - in theory - less dangerous than chances conceded through the middle. United's backline have also - under both Carrick and Amorim - struggled to track and duel with their opponents in one-against-one situations when they have committed to a full press. When using a man-to-man press, losing an individual battle, or lacking the intensity to arrive at your opposing player quickly, makes the system fall apart as we saw for Como's second goal. In the Premier League, United have also had spells during which they have attempted to press in a more man-to-man fashion, but these have also been imperfectly executed. In fact, against Spurs, it was Fernandes who misread moments and positioned himself incorrectly. What can United do? Despite Amorim's flaws, one of his strengths was in improving United's physical base and intensity. There is a question as to whether Carrick's United, with one game a week last season, were beneficiaries of that. This season they look unable to sustain the intensity to execute a man-to-man press with the effectiveness of, say, Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton - a physically fit squad aligned on how and when to press. For United, more concerningly, there appears to be a disconnect - at least in how Fernandes sees the game and the messaging from the coaching staff. This misalignment makes it hard to execute any defensive approach, with good defending built on intensity and co-ordination between players. "Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure," said Fernandes. "Take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable." But bravery is subjective and one might argue that Carrick defending with four forwards - ready to attack quickly - is an incredibly brave, if not naive, decision. Going for a 'half man-to-man' approach - looking to lock opponents into one area of the pitch - while allowing some players to defend more zonally feels like a fair trade-off from Carrick. But how United defend in the 4-2-4 feels outdated already, and is being exposed. So while both Fernandes and Carrick seem to have a point, if United are to win regularly, any solution this season is likely to lie somewhere in between their views. item.title: ‘You should be panicked’ – Stephen A. Smith worried by what he’s seen from Arch Manning
item.description: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images Arch Manning’s future as the starter for the Texas Longhorns is now coming under serious scrutiny following a second consecutive loss at the weekend. There have been a lot of people in the media questioning whether Manning is going to be ready to declare for the 2027 NFL Draft next year and, for some, the answer may be becoming clear. Things are not going to get any easier as the Longhorns face Ole Miss next. With two minutes remaining on the clock against the Florida Gators, Manning was strip-sacked whilst chasing the three-point deficit. Having only thrown for one touchdown during the game this has led to even more concerns surrounding the 22-year-old. Stephen A. Smith concerned by Arch Manning’s struggles for Texas Longhorns The Longhorns have dropped right down the rankings over the last couple of weeks following their back-to-back losses. What Smith is seeing from Manning right now is causing him a lot of concern as he does not believe the youngster is showing enough positives during these losses. “You can’t possibly talk about Arch Manning and Texas and not be in panic mode. They were number one in the nation three weeks ago. They’re at number 19 now. That is a precipitous drop-off. Why? Because you lose games,” Smith said on First Take. “Those two games that they lost, they go up against Oklahoma, the Red River Rivalry. This is why you go to Texas. This is why you go to Oklahoma for that rivalry. This brother gave up 10 points in the fourth quarter and gave up an interception. Obviously, the two interceptions he threw equated to 10 points. You cost them. “Then you turn around the next week. You get strip-sacked. You lose the ball. You’re not holding on to it. In the midst of all of this: numerous missed throws, panicking under pressure. Again, like you said, he’s been there four years. He’s no damn freshman. I mean, how long are we going to wait? Now it might not be all on him. It could be [Steve] Sarkisian.” “You should be panicked.” Whether Steve Sarkisian would actually be willing to make a change at quarterback is a completely different matter but something is going to have to change and quickly in Texas. The Longhorns are dropping like a stone and it is largely coming as a result of Manning’s struggles. A huge week lies ahead of the Longhorns as Ole Miss prepare to travel to Austin. Another loss for Manning could prove the straw that breaks the camel’s back. item.description: The Ballon d’Or ceremony is almost here with a men’s and women’s winner set to be announced in London on Monday 26 October. England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is the favourite, with Spain and Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal a close second as debate swirls around the biggest individual prize in the sport. Kane is aiming to be the first English player to win the men’s award since Michael Owen in 2001, despite lacking a continental trophy, with the 33-year-old’s gluttony for goals and assists positioning him nicely to secure a career-high honour. Rodri , the Ballon d’Or winner in 2024, won the golden ball at the World Cup after leading Spain to glory while France and Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe broke the World Cup goalscoring record after hitting an incredible 10 goals across the tournament. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who has since suffered a season-ending knee injury was absent from the World Cup but was arguably the standout player in the men’s Champions League last season after inspiring back-to-back titles for Paris Saint-Germain. When and where is the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony? The Ballon d’Or ceremony will take place in London on Monday, 26 October, with the event getting underway from 8pm GMT. You can watch the ceremony on the official website ballondor.com or DAZN, globally, with a free live stream available from both, while Independent Sport will bring you a live blog with updates, reaction and analysis. item.title: Where the Foundation for Success Lies ...
item.description: Where the Foundation for Success Lies ... Gregor Kobel kept four clean sheets in the first six matchdays. His 67 percent clean sheet rate is once again significantly higher than that of the entire previous season (44%). Conceding only four goals is a unique achievement across the league. The xGoals value for BVB’s opponents is also the lowest in the Bundesliga (4.9)—no surprise, since Borussia Dortmund has also allowed the fewest clear-cut scoring chances by opponents (only two). Kobel can rely on an exceptionally strong defensive line. New signing Joane Gadou (65.9% of challenges won), defensive leader Waldemar Anton (61.1%), and the outstanding Nico Schlotterbeck (69.5%!) form the league’s most solid defensive unit. On average, BVB’s back three win two out of every three duels (65.5%), placing them ahead of the defensive lines of their direct rivals from Munich and Freiburg in terms of success rate—though the comparison isn’t entirely apples-to-apples, since FC Bayern (53.7%) and SC Freiburg (62.9%) play with a back four. The defensive movement is also fundamentally sound across all parts of the Dortmund squad: so far, the Black and Yellows have allowed only three shots on goal by opponents following a counterattack. Only Bayern Munich is even more vigilant in this regard. Boris Rupert

BVB has come back from a 0-1 deficit to win more often against Eintracht Frankfurt than against any other team (twelve times). Borussia Dortmund has won 14 of its last 15 Bundesliga home games against Eintracht Frankfurt. In their last 29 home games against the Hessians, the Westphalians have never failed to score (the last time was in April 1991). Of the ten penalty kicks awarded in this rivalry at Strobelallee, nine went to BVB.

item.title: CBS announces final decision on Tony Romo’s replacement
item.description: Credit: Reuters Images, CBS Earlier this month, CBS announced that NFL game analyst Tony Romo’s leave from the network had officially been made permanent, ending the former quarterback’s tenure as the network’s top NFL analyst after his OWI arrest in Milwaukee over the summer. Romo hadn’t called a game this season, and his absence left CBS without the analyst it had built its NFL coverage around since 2017, when it handed the former Cowboys quarterback the No. 1 job straight out of retirement and later locked him into a 10-year, $180 million contract. “CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways. We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward,” CBS’s statement read. “J.J. Watt will continue to partner with Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on our lead NFL announce team for the rest of the season. All other teams remain the same, including Ian Eagle, Ross Tucker and Evan Washburn.” It was unclear at the time whether Watt would only continue alongside Nantz through the season, or if he would be the permanent color analyst in CBS’s top booth. On Thursday, the network announced its final decision. “JJ Watt Agrees to Multi-Year Deal to Serve as NFL ON CBS Lead Game Analyst Watt will continue to call the Network’s top games alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson as CBS Sports’ lead NFL announce team,” CBS Sports PR posted on X. “I’ve had a front-row seat to JJ’s growth as a top-tier broadcaster, watching him tackle this role just like he did his hall-of-fame playing career,” Skydance Chairman David Berson said via statement. “He’s insightful, entertaining, passionate, meticulous in his preparation, and the ultimate teammate. He has a unique ability to see things and communicate to fans of all levels. We are thrilled to have him leading our NFL coverage.” “I am incredibly honored and grateful to have the opportunity to represent CBS Sports and all of the fantastic people who make this place so special,” Watt said. “From the brotherhood of THE NFL TODAY to my crews calling games, I couldn’t ask for better teammates alongside me on this television journey. I am thankful to David Berson for his leadership, vision and trust. I love this job and can’t wait to see ya Sunday with Jim and Tracy and many more Sundays to come!” As for Romo, Nantz believes that at some point, he’ll be back in the business. “I think unquestionably he will work again,” Nantz said. “I don’t know if it’s calling games or being in studio, but he’s got a lot of talent. He’s got a lot of people who like him, and he’s a star. Rather than simply trying to put the ball in play, many hitters prioritize pitches they can drive with authority. Modern hitting instruction emphasizes exit velocity, launch angle and swing decisions — the combination of recognizing a hittable pitch and delivering a swing capable of producing damage. A fly ball hit at an optimal launch angle can clear the fence. A weak ground ball, even when successfully put into play, frequently becomes an out. But the pursuit of harder contact can create a difficult trade-off. Hitters trying to elevate the baseball may develop swings with more upward movement, while pitchers increasingly attack with high-velocity fastballs, breaking pitches and changing speeds. The result can be more home runs, but also more empty swings. White Sox hitting coach Derek Shomon acknowledged the concern while explaining that the reasons behind strikeouts matter as much as the totals. “I would be sitting here lying to you if I’m OK with strikeouts,” Shomon told MLB.com in September. “No one is.” Shomon said the organization evaluates whether strikeouts result from chasing pitches outside the zone, missing hittable strikes or making poor decisions with two strikes. A CENTURY OF CHANGING EXPECTATIONS For much of baseball history, striking out was relatively uncommon. Hitters were expected to protect the plate, shorten their swings with two strikes and make pitchers rely on their defense. Contact was considered a fundamental part of offensive success. That philosophy gradually changed as hitters and organizations began placing greater value on walks, extra-base hits and home runs. Statistical analysis reinforced the importance of reaching base and hitting for power. Meanwhile, improvements in pitching velocity, pitch design and bullpen specialization made simply putting the ball in play increasingly difficult. In 2026, major league teams averaged 8.38 strikeouts per game, compared with 8.36 in 2025, according to Baseball-Reference. Although the increase was small, the modern figures remain substantially higher than those of earlier generations. The distinction is important: Baseball is not necessarily experiencing a new annual strikeout record, but it continues operating in an era in which a team striking out eight or nine times per game is ordinary. For an individual hitter, that environment has changed the definition of an acceptable offensive performance. A player can strike out 200 times and still provide significant value through walks and home runs. For the White Sox, nobody embodied that contradiction more dramatically than Munetaka Murakami. The Japanese slugger finished with 35 home runs, 77 RBIs and 92 walks, helping anchor a White Sox lineup that scored more runs than any other American League team. But he also struck out 196 times in 454 at-bats, a staggering total for one of Chicago’s most important hitters. His struggles became especially pronounced during August. Murakami struck out 46 times that month while hitting five home runs. item.title: Raul Fernandez still compromised after Indonesia finger injury: “I’m not at 100%”
item.description: Motorsport photo Raul Fernandez has admitted he is not 100% fit heading into the Australian Grand Prix after breaking a finger in a crash at Mandalika a fortnight ago. The Trackhouse rider was unfortunate to get caught up in a first-lap incident with Aprilia’s Marco Bezzecchi during the sprint race for the Indonesian Grand Prix. The impact left him with a broken index finger on his right hand, forcing him to adapt his technique and brake using his middle finger in the following day’s race. While there were doubts over whether he would be able to take the start, he battled through pain and fought for victory against Bezzecchi, before settling for second position behind the Italian. While the short break since the Lombok event has allowed the injury to heal to some extent, Fernandez said he hasn’t fully recovered as he returns to the scene of his first grand prix victory in MotoGP. “My condition compared to last year is a little bit worse, but compared with Mandalika, it is much better,” he said at Phillip Island on Thursday. “It can be a good weekend. For sure, the condition that I have now is not 100%, so I will have to manage with the team, and then we see what we can do. “Of course, in Mandalika, I crashed on Saturday and I raced on Sunday. Here, I will race [as well]. Then we will see. “There are too many things that we cannot control. The first thing is the weather, which can change here every moment, and then we see how we can manage physically because I think this will be the more difficult thing for me.” Raul Fernandez, Trackhouse Racing Raul Fernandez, Trackhouse Racing Fernandez claimed his maiden victory at Phillip Island last year, coming from fourth on the grid to beat VR46’s Fabio di Giannantonio by 1.5s. He was also the fastest rider at the last round of the season in Indonesia, having topped practice and qualified his bike on pole position, but the finger injury sustained on Saturday derailed his bid for victory. Fernandez admitted that his victory at the 2025 Australian GP was made easier by both Marc Marquez and Jorge Martin being absent due to their own injuries, but is keen to fight for the top spot against the two title contenders this year. “I am not thinking about what position can be possible,” he said. The thing is we have to work day by day, especially to see how my finger is during the weekend. “Then, last year here Martin and Marco were not on the grid. So, it means that this year will be quite different. “Anyway, if we are on the grid, we have our chance to to fight for that [victory] and for sure we will try.” Read Also: Marc Marquez targeting “as close to 37 points as possible” at Aprilia-friendly Phillip Island “It will be so sad” - MotoGP riders lament loss of Phillip Island To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.description: GWANGJU, South Korea — Karis Davidson had six birdies in eight holes but bogeyed her ninth Thursday for a 6-under 66 and was tied for the first-round lead at the LPGA’s BMW Ladies Championship. Davidson, who started on the 10th hole Thursday, was level with Yuri Yoshida on the Pine Beach Golf Links southwest of Gwangju. Davidson and Yoshida are both seeking their first wins on the LPGA Tour. No. 3-ranked Haeran Ryu shot 67 and was tied for third. Her round included a chip-in birdie from off the fifth green. Also tied for third were Americans Lucy Li and Lauren Coughlin and European Solheim Cup player Julia Lopez Ramirez. “All I did was hit a lot of fairways, keep the approaches in a safe place and try to hole the putts,” Lopez Ramirez told the LPGA Tour website. In an effort to stay loose during her round, Lopez Ramirez said she competed at Sudoku between shots to keep her mind off golf — and she finished the puzzle. That relaxed mindset is the plan for the weekend. “The most important thing right now is just to keep having my fun and try to keep my mind in a really good place,” she said. No. 7-ranked Lottie Woad, who was on the victorious European team in the Solheim Cup, shot 69. Defending champion Sei Young Kim, who ended a five-year victory drought in 2025 with a win on the Pine Beach links, had an opening 72. Ruoning Yin, who is not in the 83-player, no-cut field this week, won last week’s tournament in Shanghai. She became the third player this season to surpass $3 million in official prize money, joining Nelly Korda ($6.2 million) and Ryu ($4.5 million). The Maybank Championship is scheduled for next week in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, the third of four events on the tour’s late-season Asian swing. It will be followed by a tournament in Japan before the LPGA returns to Florida to wrap up the season. 2026 BMW Ladies Championship: How to watch on TV, stream The BMW Ladies Championship is back at Pine Beach Golf Links this week. item.title: Vikings’ Brian Flores reacts to report of racial discrimination during his hiring process
item.description: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images Vikings’ Brian Flores reacts to report of racial discrimination during his hiring process appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is keeping his focus on football despite renewed scrutiny surrounding his racial discrimination lawsuit against the NFL. Flores addressed reporters at TCO Performance Center after an unsealed court document detailing a past Las Vegas Raiders head coaching search sparked controversy . Reported by Front Office Sports’ Daniel Kaplan, the coaching assessment was prepared by executive search firm Korn Ferry. It allegedly contained racial stereotypes and coded language when profiling Flores. The document has intensified attention on Flores’ ongoing 2022 lawsuit, which alleges discrimination in the league’s hiring practices. However, the Minnesota defensive mastermind declined to discuss the latest development . He chose instead to direct attention toward his team. “This forum is about our players, not any personal situation for me,” Flores said, according to ESPN’s Kevin Seifert. “I understand the question, respect it, but I’ll use this time to talk about our players and our coaches, our team.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) His response kept the spotlight on Minnesota’s on-field performance as the Vikings prepare for Week 7. The legal dispute remains significant. However, Flores made clear that his weekly media availability would not become a platform for discussing his personal case. Flores has built a reputation as one of the NFL’s most aggressive defensive strategists. His coaching career has spanned more than two decades. He spent 15 seasons with the New England Patriots, earning four Super Bowl rings before becoming the Miami Dolphins’ head coach in 2019. After compiling a 24-25 record in Miami, he was dismissed following the 2021 season. Flores then filed his landmark lawsuit against the NFL and multiple teams. Flores later joined Pittsburgh as a senior defensive assistant before becoming Minnesota’s defensive coordinator in 2023. His blitz-heavy schemes have helped establish the Vikings as a defensive force . His current priority remains sustaining that success while his legal challenge continues. item.title: Declan Rice says Harry Kane is the ‘clear winner’ for Ballon d’Or
item.description: Declan Rice says Harry Kane is the ‘clear winner’ for Ballon d’Or Declan Rice claimed that England teammate Harry Kane is the “clear winner” of this year’s Ballon d’Or award. Speaking to TNT Sports after Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Kane’s Bayern Munich last night, Rice praised his international team-mate, who is among the favourites to win the award given to the best player in Europe over the past year. “For me, he’s the clear winner,” Rice said. “I think his numbers speak for themselves. The year he’s had has been remarkable. “He’s obviously up against some other world-class players, but when you play with him, you realise how good he is.” Both Englishmen were on the scoresheet on Wednesday night. Eberechi Eze put Arsenal ahead after 25 minutes, but Bayern were level ten minutes later as Alphonso Davies finished from a sumptuous Kane pass. The striker scored from the spot just after the hour mark, but Rice levelled the tie on 82 minutes. Rice added: “When you play against him, you see how much of a pain it is. “I mean, as a striker, to play that pass that he did for that goal and then obviously took the penalty how he did, it’s just, yeah, he’s ridiculous. “He’s such a good player and I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him.” Kane scored 73 goals in 65 matches last season to go along with eight assists. He has taken that same red-hot form into this season. In 15 games, he has recorded 16 goals and eight assists for club & country. He is the favourite for the award ahead of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe but will have to wait until Monday’s ceremony in London to find out if he is to become the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to be honoured with the award.

item.title: Neuer moves into joint third place in Champions League appearances
item.description: Neuer moves into joint third place in Champions League appearances Manuel Neuer has moved into joint third place on the UEFA Champions League’s all-time appearances list after reaching 163 matches during Bayern Munich’s game against Arsenal . The Germany goalkeeper is now level with former Barcelona forward Lionel Messi and ex-Bayern team-mate Thomas Muller , underlining his longevity at the highest level of European football. Only two players have made more appearances in the competition’s modern era. Cristiano Ronaldo leads the rankings with 183, while former Real Madrid and Porto goalkeeper Iker Casillas is second with 177. Neuer’s latest milestone also draws him level with Müller as the German player with the most Champions League appearances. The 39-year-old began his European career at Schalke before joining Bayern in 2011. He has since become a key figure for the German club, helping them win the Champions League in 2013 and 2020. item.title: The Newcastle United players who would get in the Aston Villa team
item.description: Lewis Hall John McGinn Newcastle United V Aston Villa Premier League I just wanted to refer back to last Saturday regarding the 11 Newcastle United players who took to the pitch against the 11 Aston Villa players. A very uncomfortable first half as the visitors were by far the better team. United improved after the break and were marginally the better side I thought. However, the Newcastle United players struggled to get through a Villa defence that looked so solid with a lead to defend. That lead having been given by Manzambi , ironically a midfielder Newcastle United had been set to sign as one of their top summer targets, only for the player to stall and eventually head to Aston Villa instead. Looking back at the 1-0 United defeat… The 11 Newcastle United players who started last Saturday: Hornicek, Thiaw, Botman, Hall, Lewis Miley, Gonzalez, Willock, Joelinton, Wissa, Barnes, Fernandez-Pardo The 11 Aston Villa players who started last Saturday: Suzuki, Cash, Lindelof, Mings, Wan-Bissaka, Kamara, Joao Gomes, Alysson, Manzambi, Buendia, Jackson This is only a quick piece. I won’t bore you with any lengthy detail. Bottom line is, exactly which Newcastle United players would get in a team from the combined 22 that included the 11 Aston Villa players??? There is no doubt Aston Villa deserved to win but I do think a lot of the reaction has been way over the top from the media and many Newcastle United fans. So many injured players for United and also many who have returned to the matchday squad but not fully fit, as Matthias Jaissle made clear AHEAD of the Villa match. Joelinton came back into the team to try and give us something extra but he was clearly half-fit still. My answer would be that based on Saturday, Lewis Hall is the only Newcastle player who would 100% walk into that Villa team. When combining the 22 players, I would say usually Malick Thiaw would make the best 11 but he wasn’t great on Saturday. In the near future I would say players such as Hornicek, Gonzalez, Barnes and Wissa are all good enough to compete with those Villa players hopefully. Whilst young players such as MFP clearly need time. Aston Villa made a slow start to the season (as was the case 12 months ago) but are obviously a good team. Whether it was devolving into stagnated iso ball, getting gapped on their drives to the cup, or just a complete inability to create space and generate open looks, the Golden State offense could not buy a basket. And while their defensive identity kept them in the game all the way till the third quarter, with Tiffany Hayes and Cecilia Zandalasini giving them signs of life when they tied the game at 48-48, the offense couldn’t keep pace with Angel Reese, and the dam eventually broke. Star forward Gabby Williams was rendered an inefficient volume shooter, as she has been throughout this series, finishing with just 15 points on 5-of-18 shooting. Point guard Veronica Burton, who hasn’t seemed quite at 100% health for a while now, was passive most of the night, finishing with just three points on 1-of-7 from the field. Kiah Stokes and Kayla Thornton’s games understandably revolved around defense, but they finished with just a combined two points on 1-of-4 from the field. The bench did better as Janelle Salaün returned to form after seeing her minutes slashed in the last several playoff games, collecting 13 points on 4-of-8 shooting. And Hayes added in a juiced-up 14 points in her own right, nearly changing the tenor of the game by doing what her teammates couldn’t: punching the paint and forcing the Dream defense to collapse. Still, Salaün only played 12 minutes, as Nakase admittedly had a hard time finding a feel for the rotation as she searched for any kind of spark. And the other reserves got dusted on the defensive end, with Angel Reese making it her mission to destroy Aminata Gueye whenever the 24-year-old French center was matched on her. But the Valkyries still maintained that while the offense was hard to come by, they have to narrow in on the defensive shortcomings, with Williams saying they can’t make this loss about the offense when they allowed 97 points. And to their credit, as Nakase would later point out, Golden State was late in their rotations, poor in their communication, and let the Dream uncork their offense in transition. Simultaneously, the defense did all it could to keep the Valkyries within striking distance. It’s just that the offense could never drum up any sort of consistency to make the Dream feel any kind of pressure. Which harkens back to the hole at the center of the bagel that is the Golden State Valkyries– their offense has real, tangible limitations. And not just ones that appeared out of thin air. All season long, the one weakness of this overwhelming and magical Valkyries team has been the inability to generate good looks. Whether that’s due to them lacking an A1, a gravitational shot creator, the offensive scheme being suboptimal, or the Valkyries lacking the right personnel, the reason doesn’t really matter. The fact of the matter is, Golden State doesn’t have the firepower to keep up with a player like Reese when she’s quite literally scoring at will. And talking crazy at them while she does it. Can Golden State adjust? For the first time all season, the Valkyries have a problem that cannot be solved by their overwhelming style of defense. Even if they dial it up to a thousand, the offense as it is is not efficient nor clean enough to break the Dream’s equally demoralizing method of hounding their opponents. And of greater concern is the fact that Golden State just hasn’t had the same spunk they’ve hung their hats on during this otherworldly run to the Finals. They haven’t looked like the Valkyries. If anything, the Dream are out Valkyrie-ing the Valkyries. And Golden State knows they haven’t been themselves the last two games . “I think this game, they wanted it more than us, and that’s not who we are. That’s not who we’ve been, and that’s not how we got here. So I think we got to get a little bit more of that [discipline & fight],” Hayes said. “About us being undisciplined, we didn’t really take care of the ball. So again, very uncharacteristic of us. We got to get back to who we are. If they bring some pressure, we just got to stay together. We’ve got to not get flustered. Just giving them all up. So I think it’s us that has to make some adjustments.” The composure and iron-clad nerves they formed over the postseason are still etched into their DNA; there’s no denying that. But down 2-1 in the Finals, everything they’ve preached, everything they’ve learned, and all the confidence they seem to project will be put under the spotlight in what feels like a series-defining Game 4 on Saturday. “This is just a long series. I could be a little bit more clear on how I could make sure we’re fighting with the right units.” At the same time, it’s impossible to ignore that emotions are intense right now. item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of their aim to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
